ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: nobody left out
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Every grown colonist at home in one of the colony's groups or with a friend of their own. Proposed when two or more stand outside every group with nobody close. Asking them along, a seat kept at supper and time together all help; a newcomer arriving puts it back until they find a place too.

plain.li: Some of us eat alone, work alone and go to bed early. That isn't a choice. That's a colony that hasn't made room.
Look round the fire some evening and count who isn't there. I did, and I didn't like the number.
[lowmood] There are people here nobody would miss at supper, and they know it. I'd like that to stop being true.
[winter] Winter is long for anyone. It's longer for the ones who spend it on their own.
[lowtech] My people used to say a fire with an empty place at it burns cold. We have more than one empty place.

warm.li: Everyone here should have somewhere to go of an evening, and someone who'd come looking if they didn't.

blunt.li: Some of you don't have a single friend here. Fix it. Ask them along.

cheerful.li: I'm going to get everyone into a group if I have to drag them to the fire myself.

gloomy.li: I know what it is to be the one nobody sits next to. I wouldn't wish it on anyone here.

cold.li: People with nobody leave, or break. Either costs us more than an evening's company.

plain.li: Nobody eats alone here now unless they want to. I counted, twice.

warm.li: Every one of us has a place now. I've never been so glad to be crowded at supper.

cheerful.li: Everyone's in! Even the ones who said they didn't want to be.

gloomy.li: Everyone has someone, for now. Let's keep it that way.

cold.li: No one stands outside every group now. It should be easier to keep than it was to make.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.dayLabel: the day nobody was left out

li.label: a supper with everyone at one table

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: a season of kept promises
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Fifteen days running with no promised wish let lapse, and at least two promises kept along the way. A promise broken starts the count again. Proposed while someone still minds a promise the council broke.

plain.li: The council said it would see to something, and then it didn't. People remember that longer than they remember a feast. Let's give them something else to remember.
Fifteen days. Every promise the council makes in that time, the council keeps. Then we'll see if people start believing it again.
[lowmood] People have stopped asking the council for anything, because a no is easier to bear than a yes that comes to nothing.
[lowtech] A word given at the fire used to be as good as done. I'd like ours to be worth that again.

warm.li: Somebody was let down, and I saw their face. I'd like the next few promises to be the kind we keep.

blunt.li: Stop promising what you won't do. Then do what you promised. Fifteen days of it.

cheerful.li: A whole season of yeses that turn into real things. Imagine the mood at supper.

gloomy.li: Every broken promise makes the next one sound hollower. We're close to the bottom of that.

cold.li: Trust in the council is worth more than anything it could build. Broken promises spend it fastest.

plain.li: Fifteen days, and every promise kept. Somebody asked me for something today and actually expected to get it.

warm.li: The council kept its word all season. I've seen people smile at it again.

cheerful.li: Every single promise! I'm going to start asking for things myself.

gloomy.li: A season of promises kept. One bad week will undo it, so let's not have one.

cold.li: The council's word holds again. That is worth more than the things promised.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.dayLabel: the end of a season of kept promises

li.label: a toast to a word kept

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.label: a lighter season
ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.description: Fifteen days running with nobody at home worn down or near breaking (with the colony's feelings on). Someone worn down starts the count again. Days off, a friend's company, good food and fewer late nights all help. Proposed when someone is worn down.

plain.li: Nobody broke this season, and we called that calm. Half of us were holding on by our fingernails. I'd like a season where nobody has to.
I want fifteen days where nobody here is worn to the bone. Not lucky, just looked after.
[lowmood] Some of us are carrying more than we can for much longer. Let's put some of it down.
[winter] The dark months wear on people. Let's make sure nobody wears through.

warm.li: If you're tired, say so, and somebody will take your shift. That's all I'm asking, for half a season.

blunt.li: Too many of us are worn out. Rest them before they drop.

cheerful.li: A whole season of everyone getting enough sleep! It's never been done, as far as I know.

gloomy.li: I can see who's close to the edge, and so can you. Let's pull them back before it's too late.

cold.li: Worn-out people make mistakes, and out here mistakes are expensive. A lighter season pays for itself.

plain.li: Fifteen days and nobody worn to the bone. I slept well every night of it, and so did the others.

warm.li: We looked after each other all season. I could see it in everyone's faces this morning.

cheerful.li: Half a season of everyone feeling all right! Let's do another.

gloomy.li: A light season. They don't come often. I'm glad we had one.

cold.li: Fifteen days with nobody worn down. Fewer mistakes, too. I counted.

ColonyCouncil.AmbitionDef.dayLabel: the end of a lighter season

li.label: an easy evening by the fire
